findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkboxes, not `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: All 17 commit points are written as `- [ ] Commit: ...` checklist items (Tasks 7, 10, 12, 14, 18, 20, 22, 22a, 24, 26, 28, 31, 35, 37, 39, 40, 42). The convention is a plain `**Commit**: ...` line, never a checkbox. Their placement is good: each sits after an implementation-plus-test pair, at a working point. Only the form needs converting.

findings.title: Task 2 replaces the design's fallbacks with stop-and-ask gates, leaving the fallbacks untasked
findings.description:
The slice design already decides both spike outcomes, but Task 2 says "stop and ask the Project Manager" for each:
- **No `ResultMessage` after interrupt:** the design (Mitigation Strategies) says D7 narrows to "always mark unusable" and the design is updated.
- **A state write off the loop thread:** D5 says `StateManager` gains a per-run `threading.Lock`.

Project rules treat a PM-wait step as invalid unless a named rule requires it, so an implementer will skip the stop. Nothing then tasks the lock, and only Task 16's vague "adjust to the Task 2 spike findings" covers the interrupt case. Replace the two stops with conditional sub-items that apply the design's fallbacks.

The D5 grep will return several hits to classify in `src/squadron/pipeline` (`executor.py:1459`, `emit.py:141`, `actions/dispatch.py:361`, `actions/branch.py:46`, `actions/commit.py:59`, `actions/review.py:427,528,548`).

findings.title: Task 22a's wall-clock assertion contradicts a sentence in the design
findings.description: The design's Special Considerations says "There is still no assertion on time in tests." Task 22a adds `MAX_LISTING_S = 1.0`. The load test is correct given the restated NFR (design line 505) and the load-tier rule, so the design sentence is what should change. Add a sub-item to Task 22a, or to Task 42's design update, to amend it.

findings.title: Small design details with no explicit task item
findings.description:
- **Run-id in the process-check WARNING:** Task 9 defers it to "the caller that has it", but no later task (19, 21, 33) assigns it. The design's error table requires a WARNING naming both run and PID.
- **`sq pipelines list -v` option:** Task 27 describes the `-v` rendering in `run_views.py` but never adds the option in `cli/commands/pipelines.py`. Task 25 does this explicitly for runs.
- **Config reader call sites:** Task 8 adds the typed readers, but Tasks 13 and 15 do not say they read the interval and timeout through them (D1: "validated where it is read").
- **Task 5 success criterion:** it can only be checked after Task 6. Move the grep to Task 6.
- **Task 16 success line:** "adjust to the Task 2 spike findings" is an instruction, not a verifiable criterion.

findings.title: Task 42 mixes code and close-out under a `docs:` commit
findings.description: The walkthrough seed helper under `tests/pipeline/` is new code, but it is committed as `docs: record slice 174 verification`. Give it its own `test:` commit or fold it into an earlier one. The task also marks the slice design `status: complete` during Phase 6, before code review and Phase 7 integration.

findings.title: Success-criteria coverage
findings.description:
Every criterion maps to a task:
- **Functional:**
  - owner, heartbeat and active fields: Tasks 11–14
  - orphaned, stale and unowned in listing and wait: Tasks 19–22
  - foreground stall: Tasks 15–18
  - prune rules: Tasks 32–39
  - summary line and `-v`: Tasks 21, 25–26
  - width fitting: Tasks 23–26
  - pipelines list and show: Tasks 27–31
- **Technical:** each named test set has a matching test task (7, 10, 12, 14, 17, 18, 20, 22, 24, 31, 35, 37).
- **Integration:** Task 14 keeps the existing `sq run` / `--resume` / `--item` tests unchanged, and Tasks 22 and 26 update the 199 tests.

No scope creep found. Tasks 1, 3 and 41 are process or design-directed (Dev Approach step 8).

findings.title: Load test exists and CI gates it
findings.description: Task 22a adds `tests/load/test_run_listing_scale.py` for the restated listing NFR. Its claim that no new CI wiring is needed holds: CI runs `uv run pytest`, `pyproject.toml:82` sets `testpaths = ["tests"]`, and no marker deselects `tests/load/`. The model file `tests/load/test_usage_reader_loop.py` exists.

findings.title: Sequencing, test-with pattern and cited code locations
findings.description:
- **Order:** it follows the design's Development Approach, with no circular dependencies. `ActiveItem` is defined in Task 4 before use, `assess_liveness` (Task 9) precedes `claim` (Task 11), and the report pattern (Task 32) precedes `apply_prune` (Task 36).
- **Tests:** they follow their implementation tasks immediately or are inline.
- **Code references:** the cited lines match the code (`state.py:267`, `executor.py:390/427/576`, `run.py:251`, `sdk_session.py:218`). The design's `:217` is off by one; the task file has it right.

findings.title: Proportionality
findings.description: 43 tasks in one file fits a slice with six feature areas and about 17 touched modules. Steps point to design sections instead of dictating implementation. Tasks 15+16 and 33+34 could each be merged, but the split is harmless.
